notes_used: Re SHUDDH, Ga komal (with heavy andolan/oscillation), Ma shuddh, Pa shuddh (weak), Dha komal (with andolan), Ni komal. The andolan (oscillation) on Ga komal and Dha komal is the defining identity of this raag.

loss of confidence after serious failure

therapy_note: Darbari was created by Miyan Tansen and sung in the court of Akbar — its origin is regal, solemn, and serious. The heavy andolan (oscillation) on komal Ga is unlike any other raag in the system — it creates a sound of enormous, controlled gravity. Darbari does not comfort; it fortifies. It is the raag you engage when you need the strength of a warrior, not the solace of a mother. It does not make problems smaller — it makes the listener bigger.

notes_for_vocalist: Re in Darbari is SHUDDH (natural), not komal — this is a frequently misunderstood point. The komal notes are Ga, Dha, and Ni. The defining characteristic is the heavy andolan (oscillation/vibrato) on Ga komal and Dha komal — these notes must not be sung straight. Pa is technically present but treated as alpatva (weak). The overall pace must be extremely slow — Darbari at speed loses its identity entirely.
common_mistakes: Treating Re as komal — Darbari uses SHUDDH Re. Komal Re belongs to Todi and similar raags.
Singing Ga komal without andolan — the oscillation IS the raag's identity
Playing or singing it too fast — this raag requires extreme slowness
variant_notes: Vadi assignment varies between sources — some list Re as vadi, some list ga (komal Ga) as the most important note. The andolan style also varies by gharana — Agra, Jaipur, and Kirana all treat Darbari somewhat differently.
